data.purpose: Primary reading size — tree rows, list items, table cell values. Monospace.

label.purpose: Controls, tab labels, inline badges — one step down from Data. Monospace.

chrome.purpose: The app shell only. Never extend to panel content.

components.name: Standard Button
components.description: The canonical button — e.g. the Tree/Search/Filter/Coverage/Diff view-tab strip.
components.css: .ds-btn { background: #16213e; color: #e0e0e0; font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; padding: 3px 8px; border: 1px solid #444; border-radius: 3px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn:hover { background: #2a2a3a; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #7ec8e3; outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-btn.ds-btn--active { background: #33395a; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Search/filter/diff text fields. Disabled state drops to the Hairline background.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #16213e; color: #e0e0e0; font-family: monospace; font-size: 12px; padding: 4px 6px; border: 1px solid #444; border-radius: 3px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #666; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #7ec8e3; outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-input:disabled { background: #222; color: #666; }

components.name: FormID Link
components.description: The app's signature interaction: a monospace, underlined cross-reference to another record. Appears in nearly every panel.
components.css: .ds-formid-link { font-family: monospace; color: #7ec8e3; text-decoration: underline; cursor: pointer; } .ds-formid-link:hover { color: #a8dcf0; }

components.name: Tree / List Row
components.description: Expandable tree/list row with the app's one consistent focus signal: a left-border accent plus a background step.
components.css: .ds-row { padding: 3px 8px; font-family: monospace; font-size: 12px; background: #1e1e2e; border-left: 2px solid transparent; border-bottom: 1px solid #333; cursor: pointer; } .ds-row:hover { background: #2a2a3a; } .ds-row--focused { background: #33395a; border-left: 2px solid #7ec8e3; } .ds-row__caret { color: #aaa; margin-right: 4px; }

components.name: Coverage Badge
components.description: Inline status marker using the three-color semaphore: green for fully decoded, amber for undecoded gaps.
components.css: .ds-badge { font-family: monospace; font-size: 11px; margin-left: 6px; } .ds-badge--gap { color: #e8a838; } .ds-badge--complete { color: #c3e88d; }

narrative.overview:
FO76 ESM Viewer looks like a technician's bench for taking game data apart byte by byte, not a consumer app for browsing it. Every surface is dark, every value is set in monospace, and depth exists only as a tone-scale, never as a shadow — the same visual grammar as a debugger or hex editor, applied to Fallout 76 record data. Nothing here is decorative: color exists to carry meaning (a reference to follow, a value that's missing, a record that isn't fully decoded), and everything else recedes into a narrow band of near-black blues and grays so that meaning stands out immediately in a dense, data-heavy view.

This is a strictly utilitarian aesthetic and stays that way: it must never soften into a rounded, playful, or colorful consumer-app look, no matter what feature gets added. The tool is read constantly, for long stretches, by someone cross-referencing hundreds of records — legibility and density win over warmth every time.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black navy canvas with a five-step tonal scale doing all the work shadows would normally do
Monospace is the actual body font of the app; sans-serif appears exactly once, on the outer shell
A three-color semaphore (green / amber / red) is the only place expressive color appears
Zero border-radius above 3px, zero box-shadows, zero icon library — plain Unicode glyphs stand in for icons

rules.name: The Missing-Tint Rule
rules.body: A value absent from one file in a comparison gets a 10%-opacity Fault Red wash over its row, never a solid color swap. Solid color means "different"; translucent red means "not here at all."

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Trace Blue marks references, Signature Blue marks structure, and the green/amber/red trio marks coverage/error state. No other color is introduced for emphasis.

rules.name: The Monospace-For-Data Rule
rules.body: Anything that is a value, an ID, a signature, or raw bytes renders in monospace. Sans-serif is chrome, not content.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is a background-tone step, never a shadow. If a new state needs to read as "elevated" or "active," move it one step up the existing five-stop scale before reaching for anything else.

dos: Do set any record value, ID, signature, or raw byte content in monospace; reserve sans-serif for app chrome only.
Do build any new status indicator from the existing three-color semaphore instead of introducing a fourth meaning-color.
Do express any new hover/active/focus state as a step along the existing five-stop background scale, plus the 2px Trace Blue left-border for focus/selection specifically.
Do cap border-radius at 3px on any new rounded control.
Do converge new buttons, selects, and text inputs on the styled treatment, not the native browser default.
donts: Don't pull in an icon font or SVG icon library for a one-off glyph.
Don't treat the unstyled native <button>/<select> instances as a second intentional style — they're a known first-pass gap.
Don't soften this into a rounded, playful, or brightly colorful consumer-app look, even for a broader audience — the utilitarian workbench identity is a permanent constraint.
